evidence.detail: tool.started events carry a plain-language label; GET /api/activity lists running tasks with the current step and each earlier step's terminal status (done, failed, stopped). The conversation view polls it once a second while a task runs and shows it above the reply.

features.name: Context tokens and cache metrics
features.acceptance_criterion: Display reported token and cache-use metrics per round without inventing unavailable values.

tests: R17-049 one conversation, round by round, with cache and folds
the ChatGPT route records the cached tokens the service reports
evidence.detail: Tokens are recorded per round, and unreported cache is stored as null. round-chart.js then shows null as 0 (row.cached ?? 0).

features.remaining: Show an unreported cache count as unknown in public/round-chart.js instead of 0.

features.name: Visible compaction events
features.acceptance_criterion: Emit a visible compaction event with task continuity preserved after context reduction.

tests: an oversized conversation is compacted into a handoff summary; recent turns and the stored history stay
evidence.detail: A context.compacted run event records dropped/kept counts and estimated sizes before and after; the task continues in the same run with the summary in place.

features.name: Success checks and bounded retry handlers
features.acceptance_criterion: Fail an unsuccessful completion check and retry only within the configured attempt bound.

tests: declared completion checks are enforced with bounded retries
evidence.detail: A run may declare checks (phrases the answer must mention, a pattern, a JSON shape, workspace files that must exist). A miss is recorded as run.check_failed, the model is told what was missing and gets up to maxRetries (0 to 2) more attempts; after that the run fails with a plain reason instead of completing. Available on POST /api/run as `checks`.

features.name: Stuck-operation recovery
features.acceptance_criterion: Detect a deliberately stalled operation and perform the configured recovery with a recorded outcome.

tests: a silent model call is detected as stalled and recovered by retrying, then by falling back
a tool that never finishes is stopped after the tool time limit and the run continues
evidence.detail: A model call that streams nothing for modelStallMs (default 60 s) is aborted as stalled (model.stalled) and recovered per stallRecovery: retry (twice), then fall back to the next preset, or fail with a plain message; every decision is a model.stall_recovery event. A tool call is stopped after toolTimeoutMs (default 90 s) with a tool.stalled event and the run continues with that result.

features.name: Context-limit and truncation recovery
features.acceptance_criterion: Recover from injected context-overflow and truncated-output errors within bounded retries.

tests: oversized tool results are clipped for the model and older results shrink instead of overflowing
evidence.detail: Tool results above toolResultChars (default 12,000) are clipped for the model (full result stays in the trace, tool.result_clipped). Before each model call the context is fitted: forced compaction when over the 16,000-token limit, then older tool results shrink to a note (context.shrunk); only if it is still too long does the run stop with a plain message.

features.name: Differentiate successful receipts from failed and blocked audit events
features.acceptance_criterion: Distinguish receipt-bearing successful calls from blocked or failed audit events and reject a forged receipt.

tests: successful tool results carry receipts; edited results and made-up receipts are rejected
evidence.detail: Receipt-bearing successes are distinguished from failed, blocked and stalled tool events in the receipts view, and a forged or transplanted receipt is rejected.

features.name: Resume work from provider-neutral safe checkpoints
features.acceptance_criterion: Interrupt after a persisted completed tool result, restart and continue without replaying that completed effect.

tests: an interrupted task continues from its transcript without repeating tool actions
startup marks previously running work interrupted without replay
evidence.detail: The saved transcript is the execution cursor. Startup marks running tasks interrupted and fills unrecorded tool outcomes with an unknown-outcome result. 'Continue where it stopped' (POST /api/runs/:id/resume) starts a new run in the same conversation from that transcript with no new prompt and no replay; the model is told which outcomes are unknown (run.resumed).

features.name: Reconcile interrupted writes before retry
features.acceptance_criterion: Interrupt a write with unknown outcome and require external-state reconciliation before any automatic repeat.

tests: after an interruption, an unknown-outcome write is not repeated until the state has been checked
an interrupted task continues from its transcript without repeating tool actions
evidence.detail: When an interrupted task resumes, the runtime refuses to repeat the uncertain write and logs reconciliation.required; the same write is allowed only after files.read checks the actual state.

features.name: Durable ordered outbound delivery independent of task completion
features.acceptance_criterion: Complete a task while its channel is unavailable and deliver queued chunks in order using stable idempotency keys after reconnect.

tests: delivery ledger keeps order, never duplicates, parks dead letters and sends after reconnect
evidence.detail: Every outbound channel message (replies, scheduled results) is written to a ledger first, split into ordered chunks with stable keys (reply:<run>, schedule:<run>). Unavailable channel: chunks wait; on attach/reconnect and every 10 s they go out chat by chat in order; a repeated key is never queued twice.

features.name: Transactional queue retries and dead-letter inspection
features.acceptance_criterion: Exhaust a message's retry allowance, retain it in a visible dead-letter queue and allow an explicit retry.

tests: delivery ledger keeps order, never duplicates, parks dead letters and sends after reconnect
evidence.detail: Failed chunks back off (5 s doubling to 10 min); the fifth failure parks the chunk as dead with its last error. Settings → Channels lists waiting and dead messages with Try again (POST /api/channels/deliveries/:id/retry).

features.name: Runtime-verified task exit criteria
features.acceptance_criterion: Evaluate declared task exit criteria and report failed evidence rather than accepting a child's self-reported completion.

tests: exit criteria on a delegated task are checked by the runtime and failed evidence reaches the parent
evidence.detail: specialists.delegate and fan-out tasks accept `checks` (the run check shape); the runtime evaluates them on the child's answer, a miss fails the child with the reason and the parent receives it as unresolved with that evidence (delegation.unresolved).

features.name: Measure task accuracy energy latency and cost
features.acceptance_criterion: Run a fixed evaluation suite and report observed accuracy, latency, cost and supported energy metrics with unavailable values marked.

tests: the fixed evaluation suite records accuracy, latency and cost from real runs and marks energy unavailable
the six suites that ship are valid, load from disk, and pass on a scripted model
evidence.detail: Fixed suites report accuracy, latency, tokens and dollars. An unknown price is null and energy is unavailable.

features.name: Export task traces and service metrics
features.acceptance_criterion: Export a correlated task trace and service metric to configured observability endpoints.

tests: T2: a finished task sends its own steps, and crashes go too when asked for
U4: after a task the counters reach the owner's own collector, carrying numbers only
T1: a task's spans nest, and a sub-task sits inside the same trace
evidence.detail: Tasks send OTLP spans tagged with the run id to the owner's collector, and counters go to /v1/metrics. The metrics are totals, not tied to a trace.

features.name: Live inventory of tools and configuration readiness

evidence.detail: GET /api/tools lists the tools that exist right now with permission and readiness; closing an integration unregisters its tools and the list updates.
